answer: Agents register by proving control over a unique memory-terrace via timed cache-pigment sampling; each epoch they must return a sparrow-weight hash of random DRAM rows, forcing attackers to replicate physical latency and capacity per identity, making sybil farms cost-proportional to real hardware: each fake identity requires a dedicated DRAM bank and sustained bandwidth, so a thousand sybils need a thousand banks, turning identity into a hardware capital expense.
